bounds.domain: One resolved lock key under an output root, two threads in one process and one thread in a second process, one request per caller. One owning thread may refuse the same key and briefly hold a distinct uncontended key. The per-process mutex and the OS file lock settle separately.
bounds.conformance: Existing Python tests use real threads, real subprocesses and actual advisory file locks. They check same-key nested refusal, release after a protected body throws, cross-process exclusion and the publication decorator's single-writer behavior.
bounds.limits: No process crash, descriptor inheritance, lock-file replacement, changing path aliases, platform lock or filesystem I/O errors, cross-key cycles, unbounded waiters or Windows conformance. The lock models cooperating callers and does not prove publication durability, network-filesystem semantics or bounded waiting.

assumptions: No fairness. Same-thread refusal changes no existing lock owner.

Weak fairness of each caller's advance and nested-key release. Each owner eventually leaves its protected body, releases the OS lock and releases the process-local mutex. A protected body may throw. At most one request arrives per caller.
No fairness. An owner may retain either lock indefinitely.
